# Source comparison report

Reviewed the complete supplied source/brief, complete draft, and supplied quotation guidance. Resolved language: en_US. No translations occur. Source support only; no general editorial or mechanical review. The propositions below retain attribution: a statement that Lind says something is not an independent measurement of its truth. Negations apply to the complete stated proposition, not to a strengthened substitute.

## Source passages

S1: “Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats.”

S2: “In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings. Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately. The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information.”

S3: “It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair. No comparison with another supplier is available.”

S4: “The maintenance team designed its categories and kept telephone reporting open for residents. Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions. The trial lasted eight weeks.”

S5: “Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial.”

S6: “Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period. The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software. There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements.”

S7: “Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind, complete usable quotations:”

S8: “We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.”

S9: “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”

S10: “I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”

S11: “Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company. Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment. It is not an inference from the figures. The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs.”

S12: “The supplier approved publication of this case as supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism. All interviews occurred by email, and no physical scene, emotion or remembered dialogue is provided.”

S13 (brief): “The publisher is the supplier, Svale Systems. The customer, Elm Quay Housing, should remain the acting party.”

S14 (brief): “The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist at https://example.invalid/svale/checklist; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial.”

## Complete claim accounting

1. Draft: title, “Elm Quay brings repair reports into one shared view.” Proposition: Elm Quay brings repair reports into a shared view in the described trial. Negation: Elm Quay does not bring repair reports into a shared view in the described trial. Support ruling out the negation: S2's shared-log trial, S5's reports entered, and S10's “Having one view of the reports.” Supported; the title does not claim company-wide rollout.

2. Draft: “Elm Quay Housing tested a shared repair log in two buildings.” Proposition: Elm Quay tested a shared repair log in two buildings. Negation: Elm Quay did not test a shared repair log in two buildings. Support ruling it out: S2 and S4's completed eight-week trial. Supported.

3. Draft: “to give maintenance staff on different shifts access to the same information.” Proposition: The trial's purpose was to let maintenance staff on different shifts see the same information. Negation: Letting maintenance staff on different shifts see the same information was not the trial's purpose. Support ruling it out: S2, “The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information.” Supported intention, not a measured universal access outcome.

Negation: Elm Quay's maintenance supervisor does not say a single view of the reports helps her team. Support ruling it out: S7 and S10, “Having one view of the reports helps us.” Supported attributed assessment.

5. Draft: “but would allow more preparation time for another trial.” Proposition: In that assessment, the supervisor would allow additional preparation time if undertaking the trial again. Negation: In that assessment, the supervisor would not allow additional preparation time if undertaking the trial again. Support ruling it out: S10's complete counterfactual assessment, particularly “I would leave an extra week for preparation.” Supported; reservation survives.

6. Draft: “The trial note records a shorter assignment time.” Proposition: The trial note records a lower trial assignment-time statistic than the comparison period. Negation: The trial note does not record a lower trial assignment-time statistic than the comparison period. Support ruling it out: S6's two versus three working-day medians. 7. Draft: “but does not attribute the difference to the software.” Proposition: The trial note does not attribute the recorded assignment-time difference to the software. Negation: The trial note attributes the recorded assignment-time difference to the software. Support ruling it out: S6's explicit nonattribution. Supported. This states the note's attribution, not proof that software had no effect.

8. Draft: “Elm Quay manages 640 apartments.” Proposition: Elm Quay manages 640 apartments. Negation: Elm Quay does not manage 640 apartments. Support ruling it out: S1, with “apartments” a meaning-equivalent en_US rendering of “flats.” Supported.

Negation: Lind does not say the team spent more time reaching agreement on categories than entering the first reports. Support ruling it out: S9's identical sentence. Supported attributed comparison; no invented number of hours.

Negation: Lind does not say she would reserve time for category agreement before a next building starts. Support ruling it out: S9's identical wording, with its explicit antecedent. ## Findings and quotation assessment

F1 — Source-support finding (claim 11): “because” explicitly attributes a motive not stated by the source. The source supplies prior separate storage and the team's cross-shift information goal, but not the exact causal relationship to separate storage. Smallest supported repair: replace “because telephone reports and emails had been stored separately” with a new sentence, “Previously, telephone reports and emails had been stored separately.” Preserve the September decision and the stated purpose elsewhere.

All three quotations reproduce the supplied English words, preserving first-person ownership, relative preparation effort, conditional advice, approval, and the extra-week reservation. The second quotation changes only terminal punctuation for attribution. No quotation meaning or distinctive voice has been changed. No quotation-approval conclusion is drawn. The figures preserve assignment rather than completion, medians and working-day units, the preceding eight-week comparison, workload qualification, and explicit nonattribution. Counts are not evaluated as high or low. The account maintains the customer as acting party and the supplier in third person. No invented scene, emotion, personal experience, comparative supplier ranking, cost benefit, or satisfaction outcome occurs.

Completion status: complete. Unresolved findings: F1, pending the smallest supported repair above. All other accounted propositions are supported in their contextual scope.

# Complete source comparison

Scope: the complete current draft, including title, summary, headings, quotations, link, and publication disclosure, compared against the complete supplied source and brief. Language: en_US. Quotation guidance read in full. No translated quotations occur.

For each entry below, P reconstructs the independently checkable proposition with its operative attribution and qualifications; N is its precise negation.
